headline: Approved one-time exception letting Superintendent Chris Rosa buy burial space for himself and his family at current cemetery prices.
summary: The Board accepted the Trust Report showing $17,330.12 in May income for Perpetual Care and reviewed the Superintendent's report of 13 burials in May. The Board voted to let Superintendent Chris Rosa purchase burial space for himself and his family as a one-time exception to the Cemetery's purchasing rules, at the current price list. Trustees also discussed a possible cemetery expansion, including a presale of lots to fund a bond, and agreed to continue the discussion at the next meeting.
decisions: Approved a one-time exception to cemetery purchasing rules allowing Superintendent Chris Rosa to buy burial space for himself and his family at the current price list.

plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES OF: June 24, 2026
A meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees was held at the Forest Dale Cemetery, 150 Forest Street, Malden on 
the above date, in accordance with the Notice of Meeting, as provided in G.L. c.30A,§§ 18-25. Notice was filed with 
the City Clerk’s Office, City of Malden.
President James Tuxbury called the meeting to order at 5:00 P.M. Members present were James Tuxbury, Vincent 
Miraglia, Joseph Barriss, Sheila Fermano and Superintendent Chris Rosa.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES: The minutes of the April 15, 2026 meeting were read and upon the motion of Vincent 
Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss, the Board voted to accept the minutes as read; all were in favor.  
CARRIED
The minutes of the May 20, 2026 meeting were read and upon the motion of Joseph Barriss and seconded by 
Vincent Miragalia, the Board voted to accept the minutes as read; all were in favor. CARRIED
CORRESPONDENCE: None
TRUST REPORT: Cemetery Superintendent Chris Rosa provided the following information: The Cemetery Trust 
received income for the month of May in the amount of $17,330.12 for Perpetual Care. This money was turned over
to the Treasurer’s office to be added to the Cemetery Trust accounts. Upon the motion of Sheila Fermano and 
seconded by Joseph Barriss, the Board voted to accept the Trust Report as read; all were in favor. CARRIED
SUPERINTENDENT’S REPORT: The Superintendent’s report was received by the Trustees. Superintendent Rosa 
provided the following information: burials for the month of May were three (3) full burials in existing lots; one (1) 
new single grave; two (2) new two-grave and seven (7) cremains for a total of thirteen (13) burials.
 Superintendent Rosa said the water spickets were off except for three in designated and posted areas;
 He did not plant as many flowers as usual due to the water situation;
 Turf company had come in and sprayed throughout the Cemetery as done last year;
 The summer youth program starts on July 16th and the Cemetery was getting eight highschoolers to assist 
the crew over the summer;
 Brief discussion on tree/bush removal and repair of gate (due to a recent accident);
 July 14th is the completion date for the mausoleum construction;
 The Superintendent reminded the Trustees that the Cemetery is quickly running out of space, and he had 
concerns about the near future regarding expansion plans.
The motion to accept Superintendent’s report was made by Sheila Fermano and seconded by Vincent Miraglia; all 
were in favor. CARRIED
DISCUSSION ON BURIAL EXEMPTIONS: President Tuxbury stated because the Cemetery was running out of 
space, he requested a vote that would allow the current Superintendent the opportunity to purchase a grave for him
and his family – which would be an exception to Cemetery Rules.  He reminded all the many merits and 
accomplishments Superintendent Rosa had brought to the Cemetery and thought him deserving of a two-grave lot 
at current cost.  He was asking for a vote from the Board on this proposal. 
The following motion was made: Due to the fact the Cemetery is running out of space, motion is made to suspend  
current purchasing rules of the Cemetery to allow our current Superintendent the ability to purchase burial space for
himself and his family, subject to the Cemetery’s current price list; additionally, this action is defined as a one-time 
exception/permission, and only the current Superintendent is allowed to proceed with this purchase; furthermore, 
this is not an open-ended amendment to the Cemetery Rules and Regulations. Motion made by Sheila Fermano 
and seconded by Vincent Miraglia; all were in favor. CARRIED
James Tuxbury, President
Sheila L. Fermano, Secretary
Joseph Barris, Trustee
Vincent Miraglia, Trustee
TRUSTEES of CEMETERIES
City of Malden
150 Forest Street, Malden, MA 02148
781-322-2360
OLD BUSINESS: None
NEW BUSINESS: Cemetery Expansion was discussed. President Tuxbury said he was concerned for the shortage
of space at the Cemetery and suggested the Trustees allow him to speak with the Treasurer on the possibility of 
the city putting out an RFP (Request for Proposal) for an expansion plan. He said he wanted the Superintendent to 
procure legitimate figures on the costs, pricing, potential income generated and number of spaces. President 
Tuxbury said the Cemetery could presell a certain number of lots to pay back the bond and to sell these lots under 
existing conditions as a presale.  If possible, the amount collected from the presale would cover the costs of a 
short-term bond, if the city allowed. Much discussion on the expansion proposal along with potential engineering 
challenges.  More discussion at the next meeting.
Next meeting of the Board of Trustees: The next meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees will be held on 
Wednesday, September 16, 2026.
ADJOURMENT: All business before the Board of Trustees having been completed and upon motion of Vincent 
Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss, the meeting was adjourned at 6:00 P.M.
Respectfully submitted,
Sheila Fermano, Secretary
